steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A computer network is two or more computers and other devices connected together to share data, information, and resources.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A PAN is a network that connects devices within a very small range, typically within a few metres of an individual person.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A LAN is a network that covers a small geographical area, such as a single building, office, school, or home. LANs are typically owned and managed by the organisation that uses them.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A WAN is a network that covers a large geographical area, such as a city, country, or the whole world. WANs typically connect multiple LANs together over long distances.

steps.body: Know the three network types and their ranges For wired vs wireless, always compare security, speed, cost, and mobility Give balanced advantages AND disadvantages of networking Star topology: central hub is the single point of failure Mesh topology: no single point of failure is the key advantage The internet is a WAN, not a LAN
